situation.note: 11 years in dubai sending money home. brothers wedding, fathers heart surgery, both this year. my wife wants to go back to india. everyone needs something from me and I don't know what I need

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call a mind that won't settle, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from being the one who always provides to being the one who asks what he needs, with a mind that can finally settle.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the restlessness and the exhaustion, named without blame.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the mind that cannot settle is not broken. It is a mind that has never been given one quiet minute to rest.
week_beats.steady: You hold that a mind that has never been given one quiet minute to rest is not a mind that is broken.
week_beats.act: You try giving your mind one quiet minute to rest, and letting one person know what you need before you decide anything else.
week_beats.story: A man who has been the provider for his family for years shows you what it looks like to ask what he needs.

understanding.core_struggle: An eleven-year migrant who has been sending money home faces his father's surgery and his brother's wedding, while his wife wants to return and he no longer knows what he needs.
understanding.mirror: You send money home for eleven years, and now the phone rings with two different needs at once.
understanding.insight: You have been the one who sends, the one who pays, the one who decides. The exhaustion is not in the work. It is in having no one left to ask what you need.

queries.hook: A mind that has been the provider for eleven years and now cannot settle, with no hour of its own and no answer to what it needs. My parents are getting older far away.
queries.diagnose: When the mind is never given one quiet minute to rest, it begins to run after results it cannot hold; restlessness grows from a mind that has never been allowed to stop.
queries.steady: The mind that has never been given one quiet minute to rest is not a mind that is broken; it is a mind that has never been allowed to stop.
queries.act: Give your mind one quiet minute to rest, and let one person know what you need before you decide anything else.
queries.story: A man who has been the provider for his family for years, facing his own exhaustion and the question of what he needs, and finding the courage to ask.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.meaning: Arjuna tells Krishna that the mind is restless, turbulent and stubborn, and as hard to hold as the wind. Krishna agrees, and says that practice and letting go can train it.
verse.for_you: You have spent eleven years sending money home, and now your father's surgery and your brother's wedding have made everything feel urgent. The exhaustion is not in the work.
verse.try_today: Notice the moment you feel pulled apart, and name it aloud to yourself.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own waiting room, and the question is what you need.
asks: How do I stop my mind from racing at night?
What is the first small step I can take?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna explains the three qualities: clarity, restlessness and dullness.
verse.sanskrit: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा । रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥
verse.line: When restlessness rules: greed, constant activity, starting project after project, craving and no peace.
verse.translation: Greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness and craving: these arise when rajas increases, best of the Bharatas.
verse.why: Notice which mood is running you: clarity, restlessness or dullness.

matched.label: I can't focus, my mind is restless

prasang.title: Sattva, rajas, tamas: the three gunas
prasang.summary: Sattva binds through attachment to happiness and knowledge, rajas through craving and activity, tamas through laziness and sleep. Each shows itself in recognisable signs.
prasang.lesson: Notice which mood is running you: clarity, restlessness or dullness.

verse.meaning: Krishna is explaining the three qualities that shape a person. He tells Arjuna that when restlessness takes over, a person becomes greedy and constantly busy. They start new projects, crave things, and feel no peace. The restlessness shows itself through endless activity and wanting more. The verse says to notice which mood is running you right now: clarity, restlessness, or dullness.
verse.for_you: For eleven years, you have been the one who provides and decides. That is not a flaw. It is simply a life lived in restlessness. Your mind has not been broken. It has just never been given one quiet minute to rest.
verse.try_today: Notice where in your body you feel the restlessness today.
verse.scene_line: You are the one who has been running the project after project.
asks: How do I tell the difference between being busy and being restless?
What does clarity feel like in my own life?

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha describes the cool shade of the tree of understanding.
verse.sanskrit: यस्यामवान्तरश्रान्तो विश्राम्यति मनोमृगः । आजन्मजीर्णपथिकः पथि कोलाहलाकुलः ॥
verse.line: In its shade the tired deer of the mind rests, like a traveller worn out by a long, noisy road.
verse.translation: In its shade the deer of the mind, tired out along the way, rests: a traveller worn out since birth on a road full of noise.

matched.label: I can't focus, my mind is restless

verse.meaning: Vasishtha is speaking to Rama, who has just been told about the tree of understanding. Vasishtha describes the tree’s cool shade. In that shade, the tired deer of the mind rests, like a traveller worn out by a long, noisy road.
verse.for_you: You have been the traveller on that road for eleven years. The money, the calls, the decisions, the distance. You are worn out because there has been no shade. The mind is not broken. It is simply tired.
verse.try_today: Sit in a quiet room for five minutes and let your shoulders drop without planning the next call.
verse.scene_line: You are the traveller, and the shade is finally here.
asks: How do I rest when the calls keep coming?
Who is there to give me shade in this life?
What does my mind need that I have not given it?

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.sanskrit: योऽन्तः शीतलतां यातो यो भावेषु न मज्जति । व्यवहारी न संमूढः स शान्त इति कथ्यते ॥
verse.line: Calm is being cool inside, not drowning in things, busy with life yet clear-headed.
verse.translation: One who has become cool within, who does not drown in things, who is busy in the world yet not confused: such a person is called calm.
verse.why: Pick one of calm, clear thinking, contentment or good company. Grow it, and the others follow.

prasang.title: The four gatekeepers: calm, inquiry, contentment, good company
prasang.summary: Vasishtha tells Rama that four gatekeepers guard the door to freedom: calm, inquiry, contentment and good company. He gives a chapter to each, then says you only need to start with one, because each one strengthens the others.
prasang.lesson: Pick one of calm, clear thinking, contentment or good company. Grow it, and the others follow.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha is telling Rama how a calm person moves through the world. The sage says that true calm is not about doing nothing or turning away from life. It is about becoming cool inside, so that you do not drown in the flood of things around you. You can stay busy with your duties, with your family and your work, yet remain clear-headed. The mind does not need to be stopped or silenced. It only needs to be cooled, so that it does not boil over into confusion.
verse.for_you: You have spent eleven years sending money home, and your mind has never been given one quiet minute to rest. That does not mean your mind is broken. It means it is doing exactly what a mind does when it is never allowed to cool down.
verse.try_today: Notice the temperature of your own thoughts right now, without trying to change them.
verse.scene_line: You are a traveller worn out by a long, noisy road, and the shade is finally within reach.
asks: How do I cool a mind that has never been allowed to rest?
Can I be clear-headed while the money still needs to be sent?

verse.speaker: Rama
verse.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.
verse.sanskrit: विविक्त आसीन उपारतेन्द्रियो विनिर्जितात्मा विमलान्तराशयः । विभावयेदेकमनन्यसाधनो विज्ञानदृक्केवल आत्मसंस्थितः ॥
verse.line: Sit somewhere quiet, let the senses rest, and give your full attention to one thing.
verse.translation: Sitting in a quiet place, senses at rest, self-mastered, pure within, one should contemplate the One with undivided attention, resting in the Self.
verse.why: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

matched.label: I can't focus, my mind is restless

prasang.title: Sit quietly, keep faith
prasang.summary: Rama describes sitting in a quiet place with the senses at rest until the mind becomes like a still ocean, and tells Lakshmana that until he sees the divine everywhere, devotion keeps it alive in the heart.
prasang.lesson: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

verse.meaning: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion. Rama tells him to sit in a quiet place, let the senses rest, and give full attention to one thing. He says this quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural. The idea is to stop the scattered mind by resting the senses and focusing on one single point of attention.
verse.for_you: You have spent eleven years sending money home and keeping the house running. Rama does not tell Lakshmana to solve the world.
verse.try_today: Find one quiet minute to sit still and let your senses rest.
verse.scene_line: You sit alone and ask how to cross the sea of confusion.
asks: How do I rest my senses when the calls keep coming?
What is one thing I can give my full attention to right now?
Can I trust that quiet sitting will carry me through?

verse.speaker: Bhishma
verse.setting: Asked how a person lives long and well, Bhishma describes everyday good conduct.
verse.sanskrit: वृद्धो ज्ञातिस्तथा मित्रमनाथा च स्वसा गुरुः / कुलीनः पण्डित इति रक्ष्या निःस्वः स्वशक्तितः / गृहे वासयितव्यास्ते धन्यमायुष्यमेव च
verse.line: An aging relative, a friend in need, a sister with no support: make room for them as you can.
verse.translation: An aged relative, a friend, a sister with no one to support her, a teacher, a person of good family or learning who has fallen poor: protect them as you are able, and give them a place in your home.
verse.why: A good life is built from daily conduct: kind words, respect for elders, no mockery.

prasang.title: Bhishma on everyday conduct
prasang.summary: Asked what makes a life long and good, Bhishma answers: conduct. Be slow to anger and honest, greet your parents each morning, never mock anyone, and remember that a cruel word lodges in the heart.
prasang.lesson: A good life is built from daily conduct: kind words, respect for elders, no mockery.

verse.meaning: Bhishma is answering Yudhishthira. He has been asked what makes a life long and good. Bhishma says it is everyday conduct. He names the small, daily actions that hold a life together: kind words, respect for elders, and never mocking anyone. He also says a cruel word lodges in the heart. The point is that a good life is built from these small, steady actions, not from grand gestures.
verse.for_you: You have spent years sending money and building a life far from home. But a home is also made by who you let inside. Make room for one person today. Let them see what you need.
verse.try_today: Before you reply to the next message, take one minute of quiet rest.
verse.scene_line: You are the tired deer of the mind, worn out by the long road of providing.
asks: Can I ask my partner what they need before I tell them what I will do?

story.title: Kausalya lets Ram go
story.story_hook: His mother had waited seventeen years for this day, and it was taken from her in a morning.
story.summary: Ram's mother faints at the news and begs to come with him. Ram gently refuses, asks her to look after his grieving father, and wins her blessing for the journey.
story.lesson: Love sometimes means staying behind to care for someone else.

anchor.speaker: Ram
anchor.setting: Ram's mother wants to follow him into exile; he asks her instead to stay and look after his grieving father.
anchor.sanskrit: यथा मयि तु निष्क्रान्ते पुत्रशोकेन पार्थिवः॥ श्रमं नावाप्नुयात् किंचिदप्रमत्ता तथा कुरु। दारुणश्चाप्ययं शोको यथैनं न विनाशयेत्॥ राज्ञो वृद्धस्य सततं हितं चर समाहिता।
anchor.line: When I'm gone, look after him. Don't let his grief wear him down.
anchor.translation: Take care that when I am gone the king does not wear himself out with grief for his son, that this terrible sorrow does not destroy him. Look after the old king's welfare always.
anchor.why: Love sometimes means staying behind to care for someone else.
